title: Mexico City vs Oaxaca: Which Mexican City Should You Visit?
description: A data-backed comparison of Mexico City and Oaxaca based on Reddit discussions, real costs, food scenes, and traveler preferences.

categories.title: 🌮 Food & Dining
categories.summary: Mexico City's food scene is one of the greatest in the world. categories.title: 💰 Cost Comparison
categories.summary: Oaxaca is noticeably cheaper, especially for accommodation. A beautiful colonial guesthouse in Oaxaca with a courtyard and incredible breakfast costs what a mid-range hotel in Roma Norte runs. categories.title: 🚌 Getting Around
categories.summary: Mexico City:Use Uber (not street taxis). The Metro is excellent — 12 lines, flat fare of $0.25, and while crowded, it covers the main tourist areas efficiently. categories.title: ☀️ Best Time to Visit
categories.summary: Both cities sit at altitude — Mexico City at 2,240m above sea level, Oaxaca City at 1,550m — which moderates temperatures year-round. Neither suffers from the intense heat of Mexico's coastal and lowland regions.

categories.title: 🏨 Where to Stay

faqs.question: Should I visit Mexico City or Oaxaca first?
faqs.answer: Mexico City makes a strong first visit to Mexico — it's the most internationally connected hub, gives you a powerful introduction to Mexican history and food culture, and easy to navigate. faqs.question: Is Oaxaca or Mexico City cheaper?
faqs.answer: Oaxaca is cheaper across the board. Budget accommodation in Oaxaca City runs $15–30/night for a lovely colonial guesthouse; CDMX budget options are $20–40/night in decent areas. faqs.question: Is Mexico City safe to visit?
faqs.answer: Yes, the tourist zones of Mexico City are generally safe. Neighborhoods like Roma Norte, Condesa, Coyoacán, and Polanco are busy with travelers and locals alike, with a visible police presence. faqs.question: What is Oaxaca most famous for?
faqs.answer: Oaxaca is world-famous for three things: mole (particularly mole negro — the complex 30+ ingredient sauce), mezcal (small-batch artisanal production from the surrounding valleys), and Day of the Dead celebrations (Día de los Muertos) which are among Mexico's most elaborate and authentic. faqs.question: How many days do you need in Mexico City vs Oaxaca?
faqs.answer: Mexico City: minimum 4 days to scratch the surface, ideally 6–7 days to cover the key neighborhoods (Roma, Condesa, Coyoacán, Polanco, Historic Centre) and day trips (Teotihuacan, Xochimilco). faqs.question: Can you combine Mexico City and Oaxaca in one trip?
faqs.answer: Absolutely — this is one of Mexico's great travel combinations and highly recommended on Reddit. Aeromar and VivaAerobus fly Mexico City to Oaxaca in 55 minutes for $30–80 one-way. faqs.question: When is the best time to visit Oaxaca for Day of the Dead?
faqs.answer: Day of the Dead (Día de los Muertos) in Oaxaca falls November 1–2, with preparations and celebrations starting October 29–31.
